races.name: Betfred Tattenham Corner Stakes (Group 3) (Formerly The John Of Gaunt Stakes)

runners_data.name: Alcantor
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist whose French form on testing ground translates perfectly to these conditions with 27 days freshness
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner who won three Group 3s in France for Andre Fabre (1m, testing ground) and was a very close fourth in the Group 1 Prix du Moulin at Longchamp (1m, good to soft) last September; below-par fourth on stable debut at Leopardstown (1m, good; Listed) four weeks ago but may have needed the run; of interest if rediscovering his best French form.

runners_data.name: Never So Brave
runners_data.note: Patient type whose recent Ascot Group 1 run suggests readiness for this tactical setup after 43-day break
runners_data.spotlight: Merely mid-division in the Group 1 QEII at Ascot (1m, good) last October and again below his best on reappearance at Sandown (1m, good) in April; however, he pulled hard last time and holds leading claims if rediscovering the form of his Group 1 City Of York win (7f, good to firm) last August; mixed messages in his form regarding the suitability of slow ground.

runners_data.name: Ten Bob Tony
runners_data.note: Inconsistent hold-up horse who lost shoe last time but showed promise when fourth at Newmarket previously
runners_data.spotlight: Inconsistent and he disappointed in Listed race at Haydock (7f, good) last time; however, he reportedly lost a shoe and prior to that was an encouraging fourth on his reappearance at the Curragh (7f, soft to heavy); won this race last year (good; at its old home Haydock) and posted fine third in Group 1 Foret at Longchamp (7f, very soft) last October; player if bouncing back.

runners_data.name: Chicago Critic
runners_data.note: Needs career-best but hold-up style suits the likely lack of pace with recent 14-day turnaround
runners_data.spotlight: Short-headed in a Group 2 at Meydan (7f, good) in January but he needs a bigger performance if he's to take this and he hasn't been at the top of his game on his three starts since, most recently at the Curragh.

runners_data.name: Poet Master
runners_data.note: Lone early leader whose prominent style gets perfect scenario if uncontested after mixed 2024 season
runners_data.spotlight: Group 2 winner at the Curragh (7f, good) in July 2024 and runner-up in two 7f Group races last autumn (very soft/good); not at his best on his two runs this season but each-way claims if back on song today.

runners_data.name: Golden Mind
runners_data.note: Progressive handicapper stepping up in grade but prominent style could exploit if pressing leader
runners_data.spotlight: 5yo who won three handicaps last year (including on heavy ground) and has been better than ever in such races this season, finishing second at Musselburgh (7f, good to soft) then fourth of 28 in the Victoria Cup at Ascot (7f, good); however, he has something to find against today's opponents.

runners_data.name: Witness Stand
runners_data.note: Former Group 2 winner returning after 92-day break whose prominent style needs honest pace
runners_data.spotlight: Listed winner on soft ground who won the Group 2 Lennox Stakes at Goodwood (7f, good) last July before excellent second in the Group 2 Hungerford at Newbury (7f, good to firm) in August; he's lost his form on his last four starts but perhaps wind surgery will have done the trick; wears a first-time tongue-tie and capable of having a big say if rediscovering his best.

runners_data.name: Balmacara
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with soft ground form but needs significant improvement on recent third at Haydock
runners_data.comment: Returns from a layoff and may find that conditions place  the emphasis too much on speed
runners_data.spotlight: Listed runner-up at Sandown (1m, soft) last September and third in the same grade at Haydock (7f, good) four weeks ago on reappearance; however, he was comfortably beaten in that latest start and is 0-11 since winning novice contests at Doncaster in spring 2024 on second and third starts; up against it.

races.paceDynamic: Poet Master provides the only confirmed early pace, likely setting sustainable fractions without pressure from fellow prominent runners Golden Mind and Witness Stand who can track. The substantial hold-up brigade of Never So Brave, Alcantor, Ten Bob Tony, Chicago Critic and Balmacara creates a tactical powder keg on Epsom's unique 7f configuration. With minimal early pace and the majority held up, this sets up perfectly for patient tactics and late rushes. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can exploit the lack of early pace and finish fastest.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Heaven
scenarios.trigger: If Poet Master sets modest fractions with no pressure from the prominent duo
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows the deep closers to unleash devastating late kicks down Epsom's testing hill. Never So Brave and Alcantor get perfect setups for their preferred patient tactics.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Power Play
scenarios.trigger: If Golden Mind or Witness Stand press Poet Master early to create honest pace
scenarios.body: The increased tempo stretches the field and favours horses with tactical speed who can position closer. Golden Mind's progressive profile and Witness Stand's course-and-distance experience become crucial assets.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner's Dream
scenarios.trigger: If Poet Master gets completely uncontested fractions with all others settling
scenarios.body: The lack of any pressure allows the leader to dictate completely and kick clear before the closers can respond. Poet Master's Group 2 winning ability shines when getting his own way entirely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the large hold-up contingent gets badly placed turning for home
scenarios.body: Poor positioning and traffic problems plague the favourite types while those with better early pace avoid trouble. The tactical speed horses who avoided the scramble capitalize on cleaner passages.

watchPoints.text: Poet Master gets uncontested lead through opening two furlongs as this transforms race dynamics completely
Never So Brave and Alcantor secure clean passages turning for home as traffic problems could derail leading fancies
Golden Mind tracks prominently early as his positioning will indicate whether he presses Poet Master or settles
Witness Stand shows ring rustiness after 92-day absence as fitness could be crucial factor in finish
Any bunching or interference in final two furlongs affects the large hold-up contingent disproportionately

races.name: Princess Elizabeth Stakes (Group 3) (Fillies & Mares) (Sponsored By Chapel Down)

runners_data.name: Sparks Fly
runners_data.note: Proven front-runner with Group 3 breakthrough last autumn, the 29-day break ideal for Laura Pearson's tactical approach
runners_data.comment: Group 3 winner in France last October and might not be far away despite a 5lb penalty
runners_data.spotlight: Four-time Listed winner who made Group 3 breakthrough at Saint-Cloud (1m, very soft) last October; ran well when 2l fourth in Group 2 Huxley Stakes at Chester (10.3f, good) four weeks ago; third in this last year and a penalty shouldn't prevent her being competitive again.

runners_data.name: Pacific Mission
runners_data.note: Grade 1-placed as a juvenile with Andrew Balding's 9/63 recent record, the prominent style suits this honest pace
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up in the Group 2 May Hill at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) and the Grade 1 Breeders' Cup Juvenile Fillies Turf at Del Mar (1m, firm) last autumn; below that level when fifth in 1m York Listed race on reappearance but it's possible she simply needed the outing; player if back to her best.

runners_data.name: Shes Perfect
runners_data.note: French form hard to assess but heartbreaking demotion in French 1000 Guineas shows Group 1 ability, 35-day break manageable
runners_data.comment: Demoted to second in French 1,000 Guineas last season; respected back in trip on return
runners_data.spotlight: All three runs last season were in France; suffered a heartbreaking demotion for connections when placed second in the French 1,000 Guineas at Longchamp (1m, good) and failed to stay an extended 1m2f in the Diane at Chantilly last June; not seen again until third in 1m Goodwood Listed event five weeks ago, fading late on as if the run was needed; should be spot on now.

runners_data.name: Princess Child
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist needing strong pace to unleash finishing kick, Joseph O'Brien's 7/65 strike rate concerning
runners_data.spotlight: Group 3 winner at Tipperary (7.5f, yielding) at the end of last summer; matched that form when second in 1m Group 3 at the Curragh (soft/heavy) but needs to bounce back from a lesser effort at the Curragh last time.

runners_data.name: Breckenbrough
runners_data.note: French raider with excellent soft ground record (2-4), Mario Baratti rarely travels without confidence
runners_data.spotlight: French raider who won a 1m Saint-Cloud Listed race on soft last autumn; arrives on the back of creditable in-frame efforts in similar races at Longchamp (7f/1m) this spring; often races prominently.

runners_data.name: Love Dynasty
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 5-year-old whose soft/heavy ground record (2-3) gives her edge in these conditions
runners_data.comment: Very lightly raced; gained her 3yo win at Nottingham; open to further improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Very lightly raced 5yo who left the impression 1m2f just stretched her when fourth in Nottingham Listed race on good-ground reappearance; raced only on soft/heavy prior to that, so won't be inconvenienced however much rain arrives.

runners_data.name: Pina Sonata
runners_data.note: AW Listed winner returning after 70-day break, James Fanshawe's patient approach suggests readiness
runners_data.spotlight: Came up well short in Group 1/Listed events in the second half of 2025 but different story on Kempton AW reappearance, readily seeing off ten rivals in 1m Listed race; winner on good to soft; capable of making her presence felt, with further progress a distinct possibility after only six starts.

runners_data.name: Arisaig
runners_data.note: Smart hold-up mare closely matched with Shes Perfect on Goodwood form, Jamie Spencer booking significant
runners_data.spotlight: Smart hold-up mare who is closely matched with Shes Perfect on latest Goodwood Listed form over 1m on good; 0-6 at Listed/Group level but she's capable of a prominent showing if things fall right.

runners_data.name: Betty Clover
runners_data.note: Struggling since Listed success as 2-year-old, finished behind key rivals last time at Goodwood
runners_data.spotlight: Won a Listed race at York (5f, good) as a 2yo but she's 0-13 since and finished behind Shes Perfect and Arisaig in a Goodwood Listed event last time.

races.paceDynamic: Sparks Fly will likely lead with Pacific Mission and Shes Perfect tracking closely in the early stages, creating a controlled but genuine gallop over this testing 1m2f trip. The pace should be honest rather than extreme, with the prominent runners not under severe pressure until the climb to the line. Breckenbrough and Pina Sonata will sit handy while the hold-up quartet of Princess Child, Love Dynasty, Arisaig and Betty Clover will need the pace to develop. This sustainable pace scenario clearly favours the prominent racers who can position close to the speed without being subjected to early pressure.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Power Play
scenarios.trigger: If Sparks Fly and Pacific Mission establish a controlled lead without early pressure
scenarios.body: The honest gallop plays perfectly into the hands of those tracking the pace who can strike at the optimal moment. Sparks Fly's Group 3 breakthrough form and Pacific Mission's Grade 1 experience make them perfectly positioned to exploit this tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-up Hurricane
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely strong and the leaders tie up
scenarios.body: Princess Child and Arisaig emerge from the pack as the prominent runners fade on the climb. Their patient tactics and proven staying power at this trip allow them to capitalize when others have shot their bolt.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: French Raider Special
scenarios.trigger: If Breckenbrough's soft ground form and Listed race experience translates to Group level
scenarios.body: The Mario Baratti-trained filly exploits her excellent record on testing ground and recent form in similar company. Her 2-4 record on soft proves decisive against rivals less proven on the surface.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: AW Form Translates
scenarios.trigger: If Pina Sonata's dominant Kempton Listed win carries over to turf despite the 70-day break
scenarios.body: James Fanshawe's charge rediscovers the spark that saw her win twice on soft ground in 2024. The extended break proves beneficial rather than detrimental as she strikes from her prominent position.

watchPoints.text: Sparks Fly could get an easy lead if rivals allow her uncontested early fractions, making her very hard to peg back
Pacific Mission may need stronger pace than provided to showcase her finishing kick from prominent position
Princess Child requires genuine gallop to be effective, watch early sectionals to assess her winning chances
Breckenbrough's French form might not translate if the pace becomes stop-start rather than honest
Love Dynasty's fitness after 41-day break could be crucial given her light racing schedule

races.name: Coolmore Coronation Cup (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Jan Brueghel
runners_data.note: Only confirmed front-runner with Ryan Moore able to dictate terms, 30 days since last run ideal for peak fitness
runners_data.spotlight: High-class performer who has a record of 6-8 overall and 2-3 at Group 1 level, adding to his 2024 St Leger win when knuckling down the better to beat Calandagan in this contest (good to soft) 12 months ago; combination of cheekpieces and setting an unsuitably steady pace perhaps contributed to his King George defeat behind that rival; reappearance success in the Ormonde at Chester (1m5f, good) sets him up nicely for another Coronation Cup bid.

runners_data.name: Calandagan
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist may struggle for early position with no natural pace, but world's highest-rated horse has class to overcome
runners_data.spotlight: Superstar gelding who has a record of 222211111 since racing at Group 1 level and is the highest-rated racehorse in the world; couldn't quite get past Jan Brueghel in this race last year but turned the tables in the King George and is on an impressive roll going into another rematch with that rival; prevailed at Meydan (Sheema Classic) last time despite the race not panning out ideally; duly strongly respected, assuming the ground is okay (not certain to run if it's a slog scenario).

runners_data.name: Bay City Roller
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with strong Group 1 form on soft ground, Oisin Murphy booking significant, only 13 days since last run
runners_data.spotlight: Consistent colt whose Group 1 form is non-domestic, namely a success in Germany (1m4f, soft) last November and good second at the Curragh (10.5f, good) latest start; only a neck behind Lambourn on worse terms at Chester on reappearance, albeit with that rival rusty and likely to improve for the run, according to Ryan Moore; needs a personal best to land this prize.

runners_data.name: Lambourn
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits the tactical nature but headgear addition suggests connections have concerns about his attitude
runners_data.spotlight: Most wins on good ground but has form on soft; held on by only a neck from Bay City Roller on better terms in the Huxley (1m2f Group 2) at Chester on seasonal debut but proved game in first-time cheekpieces and, based on Ryan Moore's post-race comments, will come on for the run; notable contender in the retained headgear returned to the scene of his biggest moment, namely a clearcut success in last year's Derby (followed up in the Irish version).

runners_data.name: Convergent
runners_data.note: Progressive prominent runner with excellent soft ground record, Karl Burke's 28% strike rate notable positive
runners_data.spotlight: Scored on soft ground on debut; flopped in the German race won by Bay City Roller but otherwise progressive and overcame trouble to defy a Group 2 penalty in Group 3 contest at Newbury (1m4f, good) on seasonal debut, taking record to 5-8; about 3l behind Lambourn at Chester last term but is now in the same ball park as that opponent on ratings, with a chance of further improvement to boot; adds great interest to this race.

runners_data.name: Illinois
runners_data.note: Stablemate of Jan Brueghel will likely settle behind the leader, proven Group 1 stayer who could benefit from strong pace
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up in two Cup races last term; only a neck behind stablemate Jan Brueghel in the 2024 St Leger but was beaten about 5l by that opponent last month when bidding for a second success in the Ormonde at Chester, doing nothing to close their current ratings differential; perhaps in here to set the pace and ensure a proper test.

races.paceDynamic: Jan Brueghel will take the field along from the front with all other runners settling behind in prominent positions, creating a moderate gallop that won't be truly testing until the climb to Tattenham Corner. With no genuine hold-up horses except Calandagan, the pace will be sustainable but not slow, allowing the talented field to stay in touch throughout. The lack of early pace pressure means this becomes a tactical affair where positioning and timing matter more than stamina, heavily favouring horses that can quicken from prominent positions rather than those needing a strong gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tactical Prominent Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Jan Brueghel sets a steady tempo without early pressure from the prominent pack
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the 3f pole where class and acceleration decide the outcome. This suits the quality horses who can position handy and have a sharp turn of foot when it matters.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop Develops
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent runners press Jan Brueghel early, creating genuine pace pressure
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop plays to stamina and those who can grind out the finish on testing ground. This brings Jan Brueghel's staying power and Calandagan's class into sharp focus as others weaken.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Messy Tactical Crawl
scenarios.trigger: If Jan Brueghel goes very slowly and the prominent horses are content to wait
scenarios.body: The race becomes a dash from the turn where the best positioned horse with acceleration wins. Bay City Roller and Convergent benefit from the sprint finish while Calandagan may get caught in traffic.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Early Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Jan Brueghel gets an uncontested lead and kicks clear from 4f out
scenarios.body: The front-runner builds an unassailable advantage as the prominent horses leave their challenges too late on the demanding track. This rewards Jan Brueghel's proven front-running ability and recent form.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Calandagan gets trapped behind the wall of prominent runners - his hold-up style needs gaps that may not appear
Jan Brueghel could get an easy lead if the prominent horses are too patient early - he's proven when allowed to dictate
Bay City Roller's positioning from the gates will be crucial given his need to be handy but not caught wide on the turn
Watch for any traffic problems at Tattenham Corner where the prominent horses will be bunched together
Lambourn's headgear addition suggests attitude concerns - watch for any signs of reluctance when asked for effort

races.name: Betfred 'Dash' Handicap (Heritage Handicap)

runners_data.name: Vintage Clarets
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer dropping 11lbs from last year's fifth in this race, ideal for strong pace scenario
runners_data.comment: Not disgraced from wide draw at Chester; falling in weights; solid each-way claims
runners_data.spotlight: Prolific winner down the years and he arrives off an 11lb lower mark than when fifth in this 12 months ago; yet to shine this year (poor draw at Chester on penultimate start) but it wouldn't be a huge shock to see him fare better today.

runners_data.name: Democracy Dilemma
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner second in this race last year, faces stamina test if setting strong gallop
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner; second in this race in 2024 off 3lb higher; ran away with a 5f handicap at Haydock (good ground) last September off this mark; unable to hit the same heights since but his AW third in February was a fair run; won't be inconvenienced should there be a marked deterioration in the going but a full revival is required; visor returns having been left off latest.

runners_data.name: Stormy Impact
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits race shape perfectly, thrived late last year in similar big-field sprint
runners_data.comment: Two wins last season, including the 3yo Dash at Epsom; the strong pace will help today
runners_data.spotlight: In 2025 she took a big step forward from her seasonal return when sweeping through late to collar Lexington Blitz in the 3yo Dash on this card; also won at Wolverhampton in July (6f, AW) off 1lb higher than today; never a threat at York last month on return to action but it's not unreasonable to expect much better today and she is sure to get a strong pace to aim at.

runners_data.name: Kinswoman
runners_data.note: Prominent racer faces traffic dangers with 8 others wanting same position
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive when dropped to 5f in the second half of 2025, winning a Windsor novice (good to firm) and adding handicap wins at Chester (good to firm) and Haydock (good); unable to justify odds-on favouritism at Yarmouth (5f, good to soft) 24 days ago on her return from seven months off but it was still a solid effort and she remains capable of better; another 3lb higher today but sure to be popular.

runners_data.name: Rhythm N Hooves
runners_data.note: Prominent style but admirable campaigner gradually dropping in weights
runners_data.spotlight: Admirable campaigner who is gradually edging down the weights; type to pop up soon but perhaps in a slightly less competitive affair.

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Triton
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose limitations exposed in stronger company recently
runners_data.comment: Followed Musselburgh win with below-par run over C&D; others are more enticing
runners_data.spotlight: Saw off 11 rivals when scoring at Musselburgh in April (5f, good; Class 4) but he has had his limitations exposed in stronger company twice since; beaten only 3l at York two weeks ago but others are more appealing in today's field.

runners_data.name: King Of Light
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer ideally suited to strong pace, 36 days since last run freshens him up
runners_data.spotlight: Won a 5f handicap (good to soft; first time in tongue-tie/cheekpieces combination) at Haydock last September off a 6lb lower mark; stayed on for second behind the impressive Lexington Blitz at Goodwood on last month's return; withdrawn at York two weeks ago having got upset in the stalls (9-1 at the time of withdrawal); the more rain the better; no accessories today.

runners_data.name: Dyonisos
runners_data.note: Hold-up style benefits from expected strong gallop, yet to win for current trainer
runners_data.comment: 0-7 for current yard but has two pieces of encouraging form this year; possibilities
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to win for Ian Williams but he's down in the weights and has run well in two of his last three starts, pipped at Goodwood last month (5f, good); wouldn't be sure to confirm those placings with Dream Composer this time.

runners_data.name: Lexington Blitz
runners_data.note: Prominent racer picked off late in this race last year, gelded since
runners_data.comment: Resumed from five months off with good third at Musselburgh; likely player off same mark
runners_data.spotlight: Picked off late in the 3yo Dash 12 months ago; gelded prior to his seasonal return and he has run well on both starts in 2026, following his close third at Musselburgh with an impressive win at Goodwood five weeks ago (5f, good); a 9lb rise asks a stiffer question but he is progressive.

runners_data.name: Dream Composer
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who won this race in 2024 off higher mark for different trainer
runners_data.comment: Won at Ripon on stable/seasonal debut and remains well treated on peak form
runners_data.spotlight: Trained by James Evans when winning this race in 2024 off a 5lb higher mark (good to soft); well beaten in it last year but he arrives in good form for his new stable, winning at Ripon in April and not enjoying the cleanest run when fourth at Goodwood 15 days ago; rain won't hurt his chance and he's of obvious interest.

runners_data.name: Emperor Spirit
runners_data.note: Prominent style rarely seen on slower than good ground, appreciated return to turf
runners_data.comment: Conditions no bother and well handicapped on 2025 best; can go well fresh
runners_data.spotlight: Appreciated the return to turf when finishing second of 17 at Ascot five weeks ago; 1lb rise still leaves him on a feasible mark; rarely seen on slower than good.

runners_data.name: Betsen
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer in deeper company today after Class 4 win 16 days ago
runners_data.comment: 40-1 stable debut win hasn't been built on but this represents a drop back in grade
runners_data.spotlight: 6f AW win on his stable debut in November; added to his tally when seeing off five rivals at Chepstow 16 days ago (Class 4; 5f, good to soft); in deeper today.

runners_data.name: Another Baar
runners_data.note: Front-runner returning from 107-day break after Bahrain stint, needs to prove fitness
runners_data.spotlight: Acts on any ground; having dropped in the weights he enjoyed a revival last August/September, rattling off a four-timer (5f-5.3f); had a stint in Bahrain over the winter, unplaced on four occasions but recording a career best when winning a 5f event (good to firm) in January; looks on a tough mark back in Britain.

runners_data.name: Cindy Lou Who
runners_data.note: Prominent racer not in same form since reappearance second in Listed company
runners_data.comment: Progressive last year and reappearance Listed 2nd was better; 15lb well in; obvious claims
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive in 2025 and she took her form to a new level when second of 14 in a Bath Listed event on her reappearance (5f, good); not in the same form at Newbury (6f, good) when last seen seven weeks ago and she is now 11lb higher; others look stronger.

runners_data.name: Eclairage
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose four wins all came on Dundalk AW, turf form less convincing
runners_data.comment: 4-6 on AW, rated 8lb lower on turf, best turf runs on Flat tracks, may be best watched
runners_data.spotlight: All four wins have come on the AW at Dundalk and she wasn't beaten far in a Group 3 there on her final run in 2025; fully effective on turf and ran a cracker at Navan three weeks ago, showing her trademark early speed before being picked off late on (front two pulled 6l clear); 8lb higher today but this track should play to her strengths; chance.

runners_data.name: Almaty Star
runners_data.note: Front-runner better on AW than turf, hit with 8lb rise for last win
runners_data.comment: Wasn't for catching after setting a strong pace over C&D last time; up 8lb and in grade
runners_data.spotlight: Better on AW than turf but took advantage of a good opportunity at Yarmouth in April (5f, good); hit with an 8lb rise for that, bringing his turf and AW marks into line; blew the start back at Yarmouth last month but the stewards deemed him a non-runner due to having his head turned as the stalls opened; risky on the back of that and there are other pace influences to contend with today.

runners_data.name: Arklow Lad
runners_data.note: Prominent racer wearing cheekpieces and tongue-tie combination for first time
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced 4yo who is 2-3 for his new connections and is in with a chance
runners_data.spotlight: 2-4 since joining Mick Appleby, notably a Class 2 handicap win at Pontefract (5f, good to soft; cheekpieces first time) in April; solid run at York three weeks ago and one for whom rain would be no concern.

runners_data.name: Star Chorus
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who was slowly away with blindfold removed late last time
runners_data.comment: Needs to prove he can transfer AW form back to turf; mark has gone up in tandem
runners_data.spotlight: In good form on AW for Mike Murphy this winter, winning twice at Southwell (5f/6f); slowly away (blindfold removed late) at Goodwood two weeks ago; looks vulnerable at this level and goes without accessories this time.

runners_data.name: Rogue Enforcer
runners_data.note: Prominent racer struggled in two handicaps since arriving from French yard
runners_data.comment: Three wins in France/Italy last season but was last of 11 on recent stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: Suited by good ground or slower; won a 5f Listed race in Italy on his final start for a French yard; big prices and finished down the field in two 5f handicaps last month; dropped 7lb for his troubles but he arrives with a point to prove.

runners_data.name: Brazen Bolt
runners_data.note: Prominent racer aged 9 with solid recent efforts, won on only previous Epsom visit
runners_data.comment: Won over C&D last July and back on song when going close on return; could be bang there
runners_data.spotlight: Won big-field 5f handicaps at York and Goodwood last July; two solid efforts in defeat this season and he won on his only visit to Epsom, albeit over 7f; not impossibly treated but he wouldn't want the ground to be any slower than good.

races.paceDynamic: Democracy Dilemma, Another Baar, and Almaty Star will ensure a fierce early gallop in this 20-runner sprint, with 8 prominent racers creating significant traffic problems turning for home. The strong pace will test stamina reserves over this undulating Epsom 5f, stretching the field and creating gaps. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can find clear runs and kick late, while early leaders face being swallowed up by the field. The tactical verdict is clear: patient hold-up performers with finishing speed hold the trump card.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the three leaders go too hard and fade turning for home...
scenarios.body: The pace collapses dramatically allowing hold-up horses with finishing speed to sweep through late. Patient riders on Vintage Clarets and King Of Light can time their runs perfectly while the early pace setters tire.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the 8 prominent runners cause interference 2f out...
scenarios.body: Major scrimmaging occurs as Kinswoman, Lexington Blitz and others get squeezed, allowing patient hold-up horses with clear runs to capitalise. The strong early pace still favours closers but some prominent runners may find daylight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Sustained Strong Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If Democracy Dilemma maintains relentless pace to the line...
scenarios.body: The leaders sustain their effort better than expected, making it harder for hold-up horses to close the gap on this energy-sapping track. Prominent racers with stamina like Rhythm N Hooves can pick up the pieces from the pace setters.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Early Leaders Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is more controlled than expected early on...
scenarios.body: Another Baar and Democracy Dilemma settle better and kick again, while the prominent brigade struggle to close them down up Epsom's demanding hill. Front-runners get first run and maintain their advantage to the line.

watchPoints.text: Democracy Dilemma and Another Baar could go suicidally fast early with both needing to lead from wide draws
Kinswoman and Lexington Blitz likely to get squeezed in the prominent traffic jam turning for home
Vintage Clarets needs clear run from hold-up position in this maximum-field sprint
Stormy Impact has perfect race setup if finding gaps late like her breakthrough win last year
Another Baar's 107-day absence could tell if the pace becomes truly searching

races.name: Betfred Derby (Group 1) (No Geldings)

runners_data.name: Rebel Rocker
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist returning from 39-day break who showed strong late pace when second at big odds in the Listed Trial here
runners_data.spotlight: Strong late on to grab a maiden at Kempton (1m, AW) in November and came from last to second in the six-runner Listed Trial here (1m2f, good; 33-1) in April; hopes for the latter form seem to have been punctured and although he looks capable of better and shapes as if 1m4f will suit him well, 1m4f in something other than the Derby would seem much more realistic.

runners_data.name: Benvenuto Cellini
runners_data.note: Front-runner with excellent form including Chester Vase victory but faces tactical challenge with six other pace-setters
runners_data.spotlight: Frankel colt who was dominant in a maiden last July, a Group 2 at Leopardstown (1m) in September and Group 3 Chester Vase (12.5f, good) one month ago; his free-flowing, long-striding action was seen to good effect in those races, but not on heavy ground when third in the Group 1 Futurity at Doncaster (1m) in October; soft ground would also introduce something for him to prove but otherwise he brings strength of stamina and among the best form; if the ground is okay, a bold show looks assured.

runners_data.name: Action
runners_data.note: Aggressive leader who carries his head high and must prove his stamina beyond 10 furlongs for the first time
runners_data.spotlight: Closely related to 2025 Derby winner Lambourn; carries his head high but ended last season with a close, battling second in the Group 1 Futurity at Doncaster (1m, heavy) and front-running second in the Dante at York (10.2f, good) last month was of a similar order, albeit no match for Item in the final 1f; a disappointing, sluggish display on reappearance was his only start with tongue tied; likely to stay 1m4f, with a possible place role but it's unlikely to be more unless the new cheekpieces have a major positive effect.

runners_data.name: Item
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with strong early form but hasn't raced since September and may lack recent race fitness
runners_data.spotlight: Well on top last September in a maiden at Kempton (7f, AW) and novice at Bath (1m, good to firm); non-runner in Group 1 Futurity due to heavy going; not the easiest to settle when reappearing in Group 2 Dante at York (10.2f, good; 11-2) last month but he mastered front-running Action in the last half furlong to win it well, putting Christmas Day in the shade as well; settling a bit better (fine as 2yo) would cement claims for 1m4f but this son of Frankel won going away and brings clear potential, plus leading form and an unbeaten record.

runners_data.name: Pierre Bonnard
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won on heavy going in France and has tactical speed to adapt if the pace collapses
runners_data.spotlight: Asserted late on to finish firmly on top last October in a Group 3 at Newmarket (good to firm) and Group 1 Criterium de Saint-Cloud (very soft) and they were over 1m2f; 3yo campaign got off to a muted start but he briefly hit the front in Derby Trial at Leopardstown before James J Braddock swooped and Aidan O'Brien has stressed that he went gently with him at home until after that race; his sire and dam's sire were Derby winners (dam won 1m2f Group 1 Nassau) and he now moves up from 1m2f; he looked every inch a serious Derby contender last term and that's probably still the impression to go with.

runners_data.name: James J Braddock
runners_data.note: Prominent type who won his maiden on heavy ground and showed good form behind Christmas Day last time
runners_data.spotlight: Second start as 2yo was a 6l win in Curragh maiden (1m, heavy); never able to challenge on return in the Group 3 Ballysax won by Christmas Day and couldn't have left it any later in the Derby Trial back over Leopardstown's 1m2f (good) four weeks ago, but upstaging Pierre Bonnard so dramatically in the latter reinforces the feeling that 1m4f will suit him well; his sire's sole Group 1 win was at this trip; each-way player for trainer and jockey who won the Oaks yesterday.

runners_data.name: Christmas Day
runners_data.note: Versatile front-rank horse who handles soft conditions well and has winning form over the trip
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden success was on heavy going; Group 3 Ballysax at Leopardstown (1m2f, good to yielding) on April reappearance made it three wins in a row and his Dante third at York (10.2f, good) next time was at least as good on form; while lacking anything like the same dash as winner Item at York, and also unable to get to grips with stablemate Action, he did plug on as if 1m4f could help; it clearly needs to.

runners_data.name: Balzac
runners_data.note: Front-runner stepping up significantly in class who showed promise when third in the trial here last time
runners_data.spotlight: Novice winner whose rallying third of six in Listed race here (1m2f, good) in April suggested that longer trips would suit; tried 11.6f in the Lingfield Derby Trial (good to firm) and recorded his highest rating, but Maltese Cross and Bay Of Brilliance were just over 6l ahead of him; major work to do.

runners_data.name: Maltese Cross
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with a perfect four-from-four winning record and ideal tactical style for this pace scenario
runners_data.spotlight: Debut was on soft; all four of his races were tight finishes and he won the last three; pulled it out of the fire against useful rivals in a valuable novice event at Newbury (1m2f, good) and narrowly maintained an advantage over Bay Of Brilliance as the pair drew clear in a ding-dong battle for the Lingfield Derby Trial (11.6f, good to firm) four weeks ago; his pedigree is all about 1m4f, including with his sire and dam's sire both Derby winners, and he also shapes as if every yard today will suit; needs to pull out more again but has to be in each-way calculations.

runners_data.name: Alderman
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse returning from 49-day absence who showed strong late pace at Newbury on reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: Travelled well and challenged from the rear at Newbury (1m3f, good; 17-2) on reappearance seven weeks ago, sticking to his task manfully too while chasing home an exciting prospect at a respectful distance; a promising, scopey sort from a famous middle-distance family but his progressive form in maidens, without a win, does not make him a serious Derby contender.

runners_data.name: Bay Of Brilliance
runners_data.note: Front-runner with two wins on soft ground who faces a significant class test against Group-level opposition
runners_data.spotlight: Half-brother to smart Flat and hurdle winner Absurde; odds-on winner of a maiden at Goodwood (1m2f, soft) and novice at Redcar (1m1f, good to soft; made all) on last two starts as 2yo; pushed Maltese Cross all the way in Lingfield Derby Trial (11.6f, good to firm) and could improve on that first-time-out display; more to do but he's heading the right way.

runners_data.name: Ancient Egypt
runners_data.note: Prominent racer making his soft ground debut despite strong form on faster surfaces throughout his career
runners_data.spotlight: Frankel colt bought for 1,100,000gns as a yearling; all four races on good to firm; Beverley and Goodwood novice wins last summer before the Group 2 Royal Lodge saw a comprehensive end to his unbeaten record; he returned to Newmarket, however, with an ultimately authoritative win in a five-runner Listed race (1m2f) five weeks ago, helping to make the running; 1m4f beckons strongly after that and he's included in each-way calculations.

runners_data.name: A Taste Of Glory
runners_data.note: Front-running type with mixed form who struggled badly in Group company in France last season
runners_data.spotlight: Won a Brighton maiden and 1m2f AW handicap at Lingfield; however, he ended last season with last of ten in a French Group 1 (1m2f, very soft) and subsided rapidly to be last of six in the Lingfield Derby Trial (11.6f, good to firm; 33-1); his owner is renowned for Derby contenders who have run well at big prices, but hopes for this one may be stretching it.

runners_data.name: Poker
runners_data.note: Expensive purchase making his debut at this level with front-running tendencies but unproven stamina credentials
runners_data.spotlight: Having fetched 4,300,000gns in 2024, he is the most expensive yearling colt ever sold at auction in Europe; by Wootton Bassett out of a sister to Oaks winner Was; on the other hand, he was left nearly 9l behind by Bay Of Brilliance at Redcar (1m1f, good to soft) in October and sported cheekpieces at 10-1 when a front-running second of four to a stablemate in Haydock novice (1m4f, good to firm) in April; admirably tenacious in the latter but the dream was once of so much more.

races.paceDynamic: Item, Action, Benvenuto Cellini, Balzac, Bay Of Brilliance, A Taste Of Glory and Poker will ensure a genuine gallop from the start, with seven confirmed front-runners in a 14-runner Derby field. The pace will be strong throughout, particularly given the stamina-sapping Epsom contours and good to soft ground conditions that will test every horse's reserves. With such a large contingent of pace-setters, many will crack in the final three furlongs, setting up the race perfectly for hold-up horses and prominent racers with proven staying power to sweep past the faltering leaders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the seven front-runners maintain their aggressive early positions and set unsustainable fractions
scenarios.body: The pace will be furious through the early stages before multiple leaders tire dramatically on the testing Epsom gradients. This creates the ideal setup for classy hold-up horses like Maltese Cross and Rebel Rocker to pick off the weakening pace-setters.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Sustained Pace Battle
scenarios.trigger: If the leading group settles into a manageable rhythm while still maintaining honest fractions throughout
scenarios.body: The race becomes a test of pure class and stamina with the pace strong enough to test all runners but not collapse entirely. Prominent racers with proven Group-level form will have the tactical advantage and class to prevail.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If one or two of the pace-setters can steal crucial lengths while the others engage in early battles
scenarios.body: The winner comes from the early leaders who avoid the speed duel, with Benvenuto Cellini or Item potentially using their class to sustain the gallop. This scenario requires perfect tactical execution from the successful front-runner.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Muddle
scenarios.trigger: If the large field and numerous pace-setters create interference or uneven early fractions
scenarios.body: The race becomes scrappy with some horses getting poor runs while others find clear passages at crucial moments. Hold-up horses with the best navigation and finishing kicks will capitalize on the chaos.

watchPoints.text: Item and A Taste Of Glory could set suicidal early fractions if they engage in a speed duel from the gate
Action's high head carriage suggests he may not handle the pressure when the field closes around Tattenham Corner
Maltese Cross and Rebel Rocker positioning will be crucial as they need clear runs from their hold-up styles
Ancient Egypt faces his first test on soft ground after showing all his best form on good to firm surfaces
Pierre Bonnard and Christmas Day have the tactical pace to adapt if the early gallop becomes either too fast or too slow

races.name: Cherryfield (Croydon) Lester Piggott Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Allegresse
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with stamina questions over 1m2f but has winning experience from the front
runners_data.comment: Won two Kempton novices but beat just one in Zetland at Newmarket final run; can rebound
runners_data.spotlight: Won from the front in two Kempton novices (1m, AW); weakened out of it in a Group 3 at Newmarket (1m2f) on final 2yo run and mastered by his three rivals late on in a conditions stakes at Goodwood (1m, good; unraced on softer) on reappearance, so he does not present the most glittering case for this handicap debut, but stamina in family suggests he should stay.

runners_data.name: Starlight Time
runners_data.note: Confirmed leader returning from 212-day break which raises serious fitness concerns
runners_data.spotlight: Won a small-field maiden here (7f, good) last July on debut; well held in eighth of 26 in a valuable sales race at Newmarket (7f, good) but he was on his own through the final 1f when making most to win at 1-2 in a novice at Chelmsford (1m, AW) in November; 1m2f is plausible and he should bring potential to this seasonal and handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Savvy Disko
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits the likely strong pace scenario with recent winning form
runners_data.comment: Made the frame in two starts at Newmarket in October; each-way claims
runners_data.spotlight: Minor honours at Newmarket (7f, good) in October on first two starts; 7-1 for 12-runner novice at Lingfield (1m, AW; York Tower third) last month and always close up to win by a neck; getting up in the final strides there boosts hope for 1m2f (despite pedigree) and he's a promising newcomer to handicaps.

runners_data.name: Hell Yeah He Did
runners_data.note: Front runner who handles soft ground well but faces much stronger opposition here
runners_data.spotlight: All three turf races as 2yo were on soft or heavy, making most and rallying stoutly to win a maiden at Nottingham (1m) on final outing; gelded since; seemingly no doubt that he will still be suited by 1m2f+ and nothing to prove if the ground is testing; one to note on seasonal/handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Lake Como
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse perfectly positioned if pace collapses but unproven on soft ground
runners_data.comment: Peak AW form was not transferred to 1m turf handicaps last two starts; this track may help
runners_data.spotlight: Unraced on softer than good; found serious improvement over 7f/1m on AW but, although running respectably, he's not transferred the best of that form to 1m turf handicaps on last two outings; worth a go at this new trip.

runners_data.name: Tailgunner Joe
runners_data.note: Another hold-up runner who needs strong pace but showed Dubai form earlier this year
runners_data.spotlight: Better in Meydan campaign in December-March, including a 1m win and he shaped as if he stayed 1m1f on final start there; needs to rebound from a poor show at Newmarket (1m2f) in April and he was gelded the next day.

runners_data.name: York Tower
runners_data.note: Front runner stepping up to 1m2f for first time which may expose stamina limitations
runners_data.comment: Beaten a length in both starts late last year; extra furlong should suit; high on list
runners_data.spotlight: Second over 7f at Yarmouth (good) and Chelmsford (AW) on his only two starts as 2yo; respectable third to Savvy Disko in novice at Lingfield (1m, AW) on return last month; handicap newcomer, with plenty to suggest that 1m2f+ will suit and best days are ahead of him.

runners_data.name: Folk Pageant
runners_data.note: Leading style with recent 1m2f winning form and proven soft ground ability
runners_data.comment: One poor run from four starts; won two, including Newmarket handicap (1m2f, good); up 3lb
runners_data.spotlight: Second on good to soft on her only 2yo start; last of nine on handicap debut at Southwell (1m, AW) in April but won her other three starts this season, in 1m2f handicaps at Newmarket and Chester on last two occasions; 6lb rise is a sterner reaction since latest start but she's seen those last two races out strongly and could have more to give; major player.

runners_data.name: Pendella
runners_data.note: Makes own running but shaped like non-stayer over 1m4f at York previously
runners_data.comment: Led 3f out to 2f out before cracking behind Stoneacre Donny in 1m4f race here last week
runners_data.spotlight: Shaped like a non-stayer over 1m4f at York on turf debut in May, but reeled in only late in the day when second of ten there over 1m2f (again good ground; raised 2lb today) nine days later; ridden by Jack Nicholls last time and that performance puts her on the shortlist.

runners_data.name: Silver State
runners_data.note: Consistent front runner with soft ground win but 5lb claimer takes over riding duties
runners_data.comment: 4-6 since handicapping; turf wins on last two starts; up in class but still a key player
runners_data.spotlight: Usually ridden by Rose Dawes; won four of seven handicaps, all once visored, including from the front over 1m at Bath (good to soft) and Doncaster when returned to turf; helped to set a strong gallop when fifth of ten at Haydock latest but he needs to resume improvement and this new trip is not sure to help.

runners_data.name: Be The Standard
runners_data.note: Front runner completely unexposed on soft ground having never raced on it
runners_data.comment: 1m Thirsk novice winner who flopped when favourite for Newcastle nursery (1m, AW); gelded
runners_data.spotlight: Unraced on softer than good; flopped when favourite for five-runner nursery at Newcastle (1m, AW) in October and weakened into fifth of eight at Chester (1m4f; 5-1) on return, so his two handicap performances left plenty to be desired; back in trip today and perhaps he needed that latest run.

races.paceDynamic: Seven confirmed front runners including Starlight Time, Hell Yeah He Did, York Tower, Folk Pageant, Pendella, Silver State and Be The Standard will create a relentless gallop from the start. This aggressive pace will stretch the field and test stamina reserves over the final 2f on soft ground. The early speed battle between multiple leaders will soften them up for late closers. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses and prominent racers with proven stamina who can capitalise on the inevitable pace collapse.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the seven front runners engage in early speed duel and weaken markedly in final 2f
scenarios.body: The furious gallop will drain the leaders' stamina on testing ground, allowing patient hold-up horses with finishing kicks to sweep past tired pace-setters in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Holds Together
scenarios.trigger: If one or two leaders gain early separation and dictate more measured fractions
scenarios.body: The race becomes more tactical with sustainable pace allowing front runners to maintain their advantage, though prominent racers can still challenge if the tempo remains honest throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Moderate Early Pace
scenarios.trigger: If several front runners show early restraint creating surprisingly steady early sectionals
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows more horses to remain competitive turning in, creating a sprint finish where class and turn of foot become decisive factors over stamina.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Stalemate
scenarios.trigger: If front runners unexpectedly wait on each other creating crawling early pace
scenarios.body: Nobody wants to make the running early leading to stop-start fractions and bunched field, though this seems highly unlikely given confirmed leading tendencies of multiple runners.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Starlight Time shows early sharpness despite 212-day layoff as this could indicate hidden fitness
Monitor how aggressively the seven front runners engage in opening 2f as this will determine pace severity
Observe Lake Como's action on soft ground as he's unraced on anything softer than good
Check if Silver State settles better for Rose Dawes than usual given the inevitable strong pace
Watch Folk Pageant's stamina reserves in final 1f after recent busy campaign with four runs

races.name: HKJC World Pool Northern Dancer Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Prydwen
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with solid form but carrying top weight and hasn't won since April despite consistent efforts
runners_data.spotlight: Prolific 8yo who gained his 11th success when taking 1m4f Ripon handicap (good) in April; got a 2lb nudge after that and received a further 3lb rise after finishing fifth in 2m Group 2 in Germany four weeks ago; while that's not ideal, he's won off higher marks and won't mind how the ground is riding.

runners_data.name: Dancing In Paris
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist returning after 273-day break but has strong previous form on similar going conditions
runners_data.spotlight: He hasn't won since August 2024 but ran some fine races in defeat last season, including when second of 14 at Glorious Goodwood (1m6f, good to soft) in August; those efforts have ensured his mark is holding up, however, and he makes his comeback over a trip probably short of his best these days.

runners_data.name: Give It To Me Oj
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who acts on soft ground and can make the running if needed, recent C&D winner
runners_data.comment: Can set pace; unraced beyond 1m4f on Flat but can't be comfortably dismissed in this field
runners_data.spotlight: Acts on soft; can make the running; won six (four over hurdles, two on Flat) of seven starts in a golden spell last February-October, including over C&D in September in both the Jump Jockeys Derby (soft) and Apprentices' Derby (good); recent run over 2m at Goodwood should have teed him up nicely for what could be a plan from last year's winning yard; considered.

runners_data.name: Regal Ulixes
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with stamina questions, gelded operation seems to have helped but inconsistent this season
runners_data.spotlight: Won on soft (1m) as a 2yo; gelded after just two starts last year (included 1m2f win) and he scored off 5lb lower on AW in February; various excuses in three subsequent outings when he frequently looked as though this step back up in trip is well worth another go; respected.

runners_data.name: Lord Melbourne
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with excellent course record including wins on good to soft, proven at the trip
runners_data.comment: Last of 11 in Lingfield h'cap in February; needs to take a big step forward after a break
runners_data.spotlight: Won 23-runner November Handicap (1m4f, soft) in 2024 and he's 2-3 here (1m2f and 1m4f) including a win on good to soft last September; those are the clear positives but he's been poor in three starts at 1m2f (snow/AW/good) this year; has a tempting mark if he can stage a revival, so needs a market check.

runners_data.name: Spinning Wheel
runners_data.note: Front-running type who made all at Leicester on similar ground, progressive four-year-old
runners_data.spotlight: Unraced as a juvenile but now boasts 3-6 record, winning his first two and back on the scoresheet when making all at Leicester (1m4f, good to soft) in October; bumped into a quite well-regarded sort when second at Goodwood (1m6f, good) a fortnight ago and this unexposed 4yo looks a big contender to build on that encouraging return.

runners_data.name: Asgard's Captain
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who finished third in this race last year, regular course visitor with solid form
runners_data.spotlight: Track regular who finished third in this race (good to soft) in 2024 and stayed on from the rear to be fourth in last year's edition; also won last season's Great Metropolitan over C&D (good) and got back in the winning groove when taking Newmarket handicap three weeks ago; latter success puts him on a career-high mark but he's unlikely to be far away.

runners_data.name: Too Soon
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from yard that targets races carefully, frustrating record but has shown ability
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Ascot (1m4f) latest was his closest finish in winless period and he kept on well
runners_data.spotlight: Housed in a stable that rarely misidentifies its geese as swans, so the fact he's been highly tried on occasions is interesting; 1-14 record is therefore frustrating but the win did come here as a juvenile (8.5f, heavy) and he gets first-time cheekpieces today; suspicion he's capable of a big run with Warren Fentiman an unusual booking for the yard.

runners_data.name: Bulletin
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with extraordinary consistency record, never finished outside the frame in 15 starts
runners_data.comment: High marks for consistency but the handicapper may now have his measure
runners_data.spotlight: Extraordinarily consistent sort who is yet to finish out of the frame in 15 starts and his profile isn't short of improvement either; stays this trip, acts on good to soft (unraced on soft) and he also ran well on his only visit here; very likeable and should go well again.

runners_data.name: Max Mayhem
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning from abroad, showed something on recent British return at Kempton
runners_data.comment: Three times down the field in Bahrain for this yard; moving back up in trip should help
runners_data.spotlight: Locally trained runner who offered something to work on when seventh of 13 at Kempton (1m4f, AW) on his British return ten days ago; also has form on good to soft but latest effort still leaves him with work to do and he finished tailed off in the 2023 running of this.

runners_data.name: Night Breeze
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who won the Great Metropolitan over course and distance on good ground
runners_data.spotlight: Finished fifth in this last year and it was just his second visit to Epsom when impressively landing the five-runner Great Metropolitan over C&D (good) in April; 4lb rise (arguably could have been worse) pushes him into uncharted territory but he has won on good to soft and is a player under Billy Loughnane.

runners_data.name: Military Academy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who left Gosden yard under a cloud but has rediscovered form recently
runners_data.comment: 2nd and 3rd places early this year came in small fields and other options look more solid
runners_data.spotlight: 1m4f AW Listed winner (also acts on good to soft and softer) for the Gosdens but he left that yard under a cloud in the autumn; rediscovered some form at 1m2f on AW this winter but he's been below par on his last three starts; soft ground would enhance his cause but others are more solid.

runners_data.name: Antrim
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with poor turf record compared to all-weather form, untested on good to soft
runners_data.comment: Three wins October-January; turf form (first three runs) is nowhere near his handicap mark
runners_data.spotlight: Often a front-runner; 3-7 on AW but he's 0-4 on turf and latest third to Elsass at Hamilton (1m3f, good) was no more than respectable; untested on good to soft or worse but his pedigree may given some encouragement, as his dam is closely related to outstanding performer Enable whose 15 wins included the 2017 Oaks over C&D and four of her Group 1 wins were on softer than good.

runners_data.name: Northwest Passage
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who has shown best form on heavy/soft ground conditions
runners_data.comment: 14lb above winning mark; seemed to need recent Musselburgh comeback run/stable debut.
runners_data.spotlight: Heavy-ground romp at Salisbury (had been gelded) in September and second at Newbury (also 1m2f, soft) the following month give him a shot; however, he left Roger Teal after two runs over hurdles and will need to improve upon his two starts for new yard this spring; 5lb out of the handicap.

runners_data.name: Hengest
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has found rapid improvement for current yard, three straight handicap wins
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced 4yo who is 2-2 in handicaps and he's open to more progress; big player
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced 4yo who has swiftly found his feet for this yard; built on a big run in novice here (8.5f, good) in April by going unbeaten in his three handicaps (1m2f and 11.5f, good/good to firm), penalised on the last two occasions; now bumped up markedly in grade (2lb wrong) and softer ground would pose a query but there's no telling where this improvement will end up.

runners_data.name: Gordon Grey
runners_data.note: Front-running specialist with exceptional 3-4 course record including two Ladies' Derby victories
runners_data.comment: In career-best form last year; third in Bahrain latest but up against unexposed sorts now
runners_data.spotlight: The second runner for local trainer George Baker and this one has an enviable 3-4 record here, having picked up two Ladies' Derbys (2024 and 2025) in addition to the Amateurs' Derby last year when trained by Ben Brookhouse; not discounted on that score but this is a good bit hotter than those events; refitted tongue-tie could be a plus.

runners_data.name: Elsass
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who has improved significantly since being gelded, two wins from two starts
runners_data.comment: Inconsistent in his seven handicaps but he's won two of them, including 2026 reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: Previously susceptible to the odd stinker but he's 2-2 since being gelded, scoring at Southwell (AW) in April and Hamilton (again 1m3f, good) three weeks ago; 8lb rise in a much tougher contest demands more but maybe he's putting it all together now.

races.paceDynamic: Antrim and Gordon Grey are the confirmed front-runners who will contest the early lead, with Give It To Me Oj also capable of pressing from a prominent position. These pace-setters should create an honest gallop over the extended trip, particularly with Gordon Grey's strong course record adding urgency. The large field of 17 runners includes numerous hold-up specialists like Dancing In Paris, Regal Ulixes, and Bulletin who will rely on the pace being strong enough to set up their finishing kicks. This race shape clearly favours the hold-up horses and those with proven stamina reserves who can capitalize on a searching gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Antrim and Gordon Grey engage in a genuine speed duel through the first mile
scenarios.body: The sustained pace will stretch the field and play into the hands of horses with proven finishing kicks who can stay the extended trip. Dancing In Paris and Bulletin have the profiles to benefit most from this tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Suits Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners settle into a more conservative rhythm without serious pressure
scenarios.body: The race becomes more tactical and allows prominent racers like Spinning Wheel and Lord Melbourne to stay closer and use their tactical speed. These horses can position perfectly without being asked serious stamina questions.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Splits Favor Course Specialists
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is steady until the home turn when jockeys start to make serious moves
scenarios.body: Gordon Grey and Night Breeze can use their superior course knowledge to find the best racing room and position. Their proven Epsom form becomes the decisive factor in a bunched finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If the main pace angle fails to materialize and one leader gets an easy time
scenarios.body: Give It To Me Oj or Hengest could steal a march if allowed to dictate terms without serious pressure from the back. The soft conditions favor these horses who have shown they can make all when given the opportunity.

watchPoints.text: Watch for Antrim and Gordon Grey to engage too early as both are natural front-runners who could compromise each other
Monitor Dancing In Paris closely given the 273-day absence despite the yard's patient approach with this horse
Keep an eye on the pace through the first six furlongs as it will determine whether closers get their optimal setup
Watch for trouble in running with 17 runners over this trip, particularly affecting the hold-up horses drawn wide
Observe how Hengest handles the step up in class after three wins in lesser company for his current connections

races.name: JRA Tokyo Trophy Handicap

runners_data.name: Kylian
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner whose form has dipped in last two starts, taking record for current yard to 0-5
runners_data.comment: 0-4 this term for new stable but this looks easier than latest assignment
runners_data.spotlight: Form has dipped in last two starts, taking record for current yard to 0-5; doesn't look as if he's about to prevail in this warm affair.

runners_data.name: Invictus Gold
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose latest effort compromised by early trouble, most success comes at Newmarket
runners_data.spotlight: Useful sort whose latest effort is best forgiven (chance compromised by early trouble); however, he has something to prove away from Newmarket, where most of his turf form lies.

runners_data.name: Fine Interview
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner well suited by soft ground with 6-9 record on similar conditions, ten weeks since last win
runners_data.spotlight: Well suited by soft/good to soft ground; has a record of 3-4 since wearing cheekpieces, most recently winning at Doncaster (6f) ten weeks ago; respected in the retained headgear, with further progress possible.

runners_data.name: Apollo One
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who acts on any ground, twice placed in this race and ran okay at Newmarket last time
runners_data.spotlight: Acts on any ground; ran okay behind younger rivals at Newmarket last time; losing run is mounting up but he has been placed in this race twice, finishing second in 2023 and third in 2024; again has each-way hopes.

runners_data.name: Saint Lawrence
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse showing resurgent form with close second at Ascot on stable debut, 29 days since last run
runners_data.spotlight: Proved resurgent with close second at Ascot (6f, good) on stable/seasonal debut; defied a stone higher mark in the Wokingham three years ago and has possibilities even though he hasn't won since.

runners_data.name: Partisan Hero
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner unproven on soft ground but registering first sprint win at York last time
runners_data.spotlight: Unproven on soft/heavy ground; has got faster over time and prevailed narrowly at York (5f, good) most recently, registering a first sprint win; peaking at the right time and record of 2-2 at Epsom (7f) includes a success at this meeting 12 months ago; major player.

runners_data.name: Gold Star Hero
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with 4-5 AW record since gelding, needs to transfer form back to turf having gone 1-11 on grass
runners_data.spotlight: Record of 4-5 on AW features a hat-trick since being gelded; chance depends on whether he can transfer the form back to turf; only 1-11 in this sphere and he is 16lb higher than last attempt.

runners_data.name: Sondad
runners_data.note: Prominent runner versatile on ground who won this contest last year off 7lb lower mark, likely needed York reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: Versatile as regards ground; broadly consistent form last term featured a success (off 7lb lower) in this contest; likely needed his York reappearance; interesting back here with that outing under his belt.

runners_data.name: Roman Dragon
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with all eight domestic wins at Chester, Epsom unknown and conceding weight all round
runners_data.comment: Eighth course win when scoring over 5f three weeks ago; having a rare 7f run; vulnerable
runners_data.spotlight: Has gained all eight domestic wins at Chester, the most recent on penultimate start; Epsom is an unknown and he's on a difficult mark, conceding weight all round to boot.

runners_data.name: Solar Aclaim
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who needs soft/heavy ground ideally, two poor efforts on good ground this term
runners_data.comment: Not beaten entirely by 7.5f trip on reappearance but is still seeking first win beyond 6f
runners_data.spotlight: Two duck eggs on good ground this term; ideally needs soft/heavy, so chance depends on the weather; favourably handicapped off 4lb below last winning mark.

runners_data.name: Badri
runners_data.note: Hold-up veteran who won this race in 2023, still useful after Redcar success last time at age 9
runners_data.comment: First Class 4 run since August 2022; in better form than his figures suggest; contender
runners_data.spotlight: The oldest contender in this field but he's still quite useful and prevailed at Redcar (6f) most recently; record in this race includes a success in 2023 (off 6lb higher) and 1l third in 2025; may remain competitive.

runners_data.name: Eye Of Dubai
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with ability but ran below expectations in this race last year, reappearance duck egg concerning
runners_data.spotlight: Has the ability to take a serious hand but he ran well below market expectations in this race last year and another reappearance duck egg doesn't augur well; has shown peak form in autumn months.

runners_data.name: Twilight Jet
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won by 4 lengths last Saturday, raised 12lb but still well treated on best form
runners_data.comment: Well backed when winning over C&D 12 days ago; there's every chance he can defy a 3lb rise
runners_data.spotlight: Won by 4l last Saturday to complete a Lingfield turf double; raised a whopping 12lb but is still well treated on best form, which includes close second (off 4lb higher) in this contest in 2025; fighting chance.

runners_data.name: Strike Red
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has lost form since April success, beaten in this race for last three years
runners_data.comment: Won at Leicester last month and a high draw proved to be a negative at York last time
runners_data.spotlight: Has lost his form a bit in two starts since an April success and is far from certain to raise his game much, having been beaten in this race for the last three years (finishing positions 756).

runners_data.name: Topwarrior
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 225-day absence, won in blinkers at Newbury on soft ground last year
runners_data.spotlight: Record of 2-9 in his first season last year, winning in blinkers at Newbury (6f, soft) final outing; may improve further this term; a possible danger, provided the removal of headgear doesn't backfire.

runners_data.name: Purest Time
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who won at Windsor on turf return, first success since joining Ian Williams
runners_data.comment: On a good mark but consistency an issue; others are safer but too much ability to discount
runners_data.spotlight: Prevailed at Windsor (6f, good to firm) most recently, proving suited by the return to turf from AW and belatedly registering a first win since joining Ian Williams, who has landed this prize twice in the last decade; one for the shortlist kept to this sphere.

races.paceDynamic: Partisan Hero is the only confirmed front runner and should get an uncontested lead at a sustainable gallop over this sharp 6f trip. With Apollo One, Gold Star Hero, Sondad, Solar Aclaim, Eye Of Dubai, Twilight Jet and Topwarrior all likely to settle prominently behind him, there will be decent pace through the middle sections but no early pressure on the leader. The large field of hold-up horses including Roman Dragon, Fine Interview, Invictus Gold, Kylian, Saint Lawrence, Badri, Strike Red and Purest Time will be relying on the pace collapsing in the final 2f. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can track the pace and strike turning for home, as the hold-up brigade face a difficult task getting through traffic in a 16-runner handicap over this minimum trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners settle kindly behind Partisan Hero's honest gallop
scenarios.body: The trackers will have first run on the field turning in while the hold-up horses struggle for room in the large field. Apollo One, Gold Star Hero and Twilight Jet can all quicken from ideal positions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays Strong
scenarios.trigger: If Partisan Hero maintains his kick despite the soft ground concerns
scenarios.body: The leader's honest gallop and lack of early pressure allows him to find extra in the final furlong. Topwarrior and Eye Of Dubai could emerge from the pack but arrive too late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Heroes Find Gaps
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses and clear runs appear for the back markers
scenarios.body: Fine Interview and Roman Dragon have the class to reel in a weakening field if they avoid traffic problems. The soft ground suits Fine Interview's profile perfectly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Favours Outsiders
scenarios.trigger: If the 16-runner field creates a messy pace with multiple hard-luck stories
scenarios.body: Saint Lawrence or Purest Time could benefit from a stop-start gallop that negates the prominent runners' positional advantage. Recent winners often find improvement in these competitive handicaps.

watchPoints.text: Partisan Hero faces soft ground for first time despite being the only confirmed leader in a 16-runner field
Gold Star Hero needs to prove AW form transfers to turf having managed just 1-11 record on grass
Topwarrior returns from 225-day break but Ralph Beckett horses can be ready first time and he won on soft ground before
Fine Interview has strong soft ground form but faces traffic problems from hold-up position in large field
Apollo One has been placed twice in this race previously and should get prominent position from draw
